| **B1: Individual Stock Technical Deep-Dive** | On-demand | High | Multi-timeframe OHLCV (daily/weekly/monthly), historical patterns | Partial — computation automated, interpretation needs Claude AI | Replaces manual chart reading; provides structured analysis report |
| **B2: Sector/Industry Comparative Analysis** | Weekly-Monthly | High | All stocks within sector, sector index, relative performance | High — fully automatable ranking/scoring | Identifies strongest stocks within strongest sectors |
| **B3: Market Breadth & Technical Health** | Daily-Weekly | Medium | Advance/decline data, new highs/lows, % above MAs | High — fully automatable | Market timing context; avoids buying in weak markets |
| **B4: Historical Pattern Backtesting** | Ad-hoc | Very High | Years of historical data, pattern recognition engine | Medium — computation automated, strategy design needs human | Validates that the scoring system actually predicts outcomes |

### Category C: Alert/Monitoring Workflows

| Scenario | Frequency | Complexity | Data Requirements | Automation Potential | Value Delivered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **C1: Completeness Score Threshold Alert** | Continuous/Daily | Medium | Updated scores, configurable thresholds | High — fully automatable with cron/launchd | The "notification" version of A2; push-based rather than pull-based |
| **C2: Volume Spike Detection** | Daily | Low-Medium | Daily volume vs. historical average | High | Early warning of 세력 activity; time-sensitive |
| **C3: Moving Average Crossover Alerts** | Daily | Low | MA calculations | High | Classic signal detection; widely understood |
| **C4: Relative Strength Ranking Changes** | Weekly | Medium | Full universe RS calculation | High | Catches momentum shifts before breakout |

### Category D: Custom/Advanced Workflows

| Scenario | Frequency | Complexity | Data Requirements | Automation Potential | Value Delivered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **D1: Custom Indicator Development** | Ad-hoc | Very High | Raw OHLCV, Python dev environment | Low — inherently creative/experimental | Enables power users to extend the system |
| **D2: Multi-Timeframe Analysis** | Daily-Weekly | High | Daily, weekly, monthly OHLCV (same stock) | High — computation automated | Provides confirmation across timeframes; reduces false signals |
| **D3: Correlation/Pair Analysis** | Ad-hoc | High | Multiple stock series, statistical computation | Medium | Portfolio diversification; pairs trading opportunities |
| **D4: Export to External Tools** | On-demand | Low-Medium | Computed scores and data | High | CSV/Excel/Google Sheets integration; bridges to brokerage tools |

## 3. Alternative Tools & Methods Investigation

### Category A: Korean Brokerage Built-in Screeners

**Kiwoom Securities HeroesWorld (키움증권 영웅문 조건검색)**
- Strengths: Real-time data, direct order execution integration, up to 20 combinable indicators (technical + fundamental + pattern + ranking), "조건검색시그널" for real-time alerts, and "영웅검색" AI-powered search
- Weaknesses: (1) System capacity limits during volatile markets — orders can be omitted/delayed. (2) Maximum 20 indicator combinations. (3) Based only on KRX market data. (4) Real-time indicator conditions may return zero results. (5) Windows-only HTS. (6) Cannot implement custom composite scoring. (7) No export API for programmatic use of results
- Cost: Free with brokerage account
- Local execution: Windows only (HTS); mobile app available
- Relationship to our system: **COMPLEMENT** — Kiwoom excels at real-time order execution but cannot implement the custom "technical completeness" scoring methodology. Our system provides the scoring/analysis layer; Kiwoom provides the execution layer

**Samsung Securities POP (삼성증권), NH Investment (NH투자증권 나무), Mirae Asset (미래에셋증권)**
- All provide similar condition-search capabilities
- Samsung offers POP HTS (general) and POP DTS (professional)
- NH offers automated RP purchase; Mirae Asset is known for fast response
- None offer REST API; Korea Investment & Securities (한국투자증권) is the **only** Korean brokerage offering a public REST API
- Relationship: **COMPLEMENT** for the same reasons as Kiwoom

### Category B: Korean Financial Data Platforms

**Naver Finance (네이버 증권)**
- Strengths: Free, comprehensive coverage of all KOSPI/KOSDAQ stocks, real-time quotes, basic screening filters, widely used
- Weaknesses: No custom scoring, limited technical indicator combinations, no API (web scraping needed and fragile), no export, no automation
- Cost: Free
- Relationship: **Our system REPLACES Naver's basic screening** while using Naver as a potential data source (via pykrx's Naver scraping)

**Hankyung Screener (한경닷컴 스크리너) and FnGuide Screener**
- Strengths: Professional-grade fundamental screening, customizable filters
- Weaknesses: Primarily fundamental, not technical-analysis-focused; web-only, no API
- Cost: Free (basic) / Paid (premium features)
- Relationship: **COMPLEMENT** — these focus on fundamentals, our system focuses on technicals

**KRX Data Marketplace (한국거래소 데이터 마켓플레이스)**
- Strengths: Official exchange data, comprehensive (OHLCV, indices, short selling, investor breakdown, ETF), KRX Open API available
- Weaknesses: API call limit of 10,000/day, requires registration, raw data only (no analysis)
- Cost: Free (with registration)
- Relationship: **DATA SOURCE** — potentially a primary data source for our system

### Category C: Python-Based Open Source Tools

**pykrx (sharebook-kr/pykrx)**
- Strengths: KRX + Naver data scraping, KOSPI/KOSDAQ/KONEX support, OHLCV + financial statements + investor supply/demand + short selling data, adjusted/unadjusted prices, Python-native
- Weaknesses: Scraping-based (fragile if source HTML changes), ~4 hours for 3 years of all-stock data, ~1 min per stock for 20 years, no built-in technical indicators
- Cost: Free (MIT license)
- Local execution: Fully local
- Relationship: **PRIMARY DATA COLLECTION LAYER** for our system

**pykrx-mcp (sharebook-kr/pykrx-mcp)**
- Strengths: MCP server wrapping pykrx, directly usable from Claude Desktop/Claude Code, natural language queries for stock data
- Weaknesses: Inherits pykrx's speed limitations, MCP overhead, no batch processing optimization for 2,500 stocks
- Cost: Free (MIT license)
- Relationship: **CRITICAL INTEGRATION POINT** — this is the bridge between Claude Code and Korean stock data

**FinanceDataReader (FDR)**
- Strengths: Multi-source (Yahoo, Naver, KRX), global coverage, both adjusted and unadjusted prices, easy API
- Weaknesses: Yahoo source can be unreliable for Korean stocks, no investor supply/demand data, no short selling data
- Cost: Free
- Relationship: **ALTERNATIVE/BACKUP data layer** — pykrx is more comprehensive for Korean-specific data

**Technical Indicator Libraries**
- **TA-Lib**: 150+ indicators, C-based (fast), well-established; requires compilation on macOS
- **pandas-ta**: 130+ indicators, pure Python, easier installation, Pandas-native
- **ta (Technical Analysis Library in Python)**: Clean documentation, Pandas-native
- Relationship: **CORE COMPUTATION LAYER** — pandas-ta is recommended for ease of installation on macOS

**Existing GitHub Projects**
- **hyunyulhenry/quant_py**: Korean quant investing cookbook; good reference for data collection patterns
- **koreainvestment/open-trading-api**: Korea Investment Securities official samples with LLM integration
- **E-know/AutoKStock**: Auto-trading system
- **KORStockScan**: AI-based KOSPI quant auto-trading with Kiwoom REST API
- Relationship: **REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATIONS** — none fully implement "technical completeness" scoring

**Korean Stock MCP Servers (already existing)**

- **Mrbaeksang/korea-stock-analyzer-mcp**: 6 investment guru strategies (Buffett, Lynch, Graham, Greenblatt, Fisher, Templeton), PER/PBR/EPS/ROE + MA/RSI/MACD
- Relationship: **COMPLEMENT/EXTEND** — Mrbaeksang's MCP has basic technical indicators but not the full completeness scoring methodology. Could be a foundation to build upon

### Category D: Commercial Tools

**TradingView**
- Strengths: Best-in-class charting, Pine Script for custom indicators, built-in screener for Korean stocks (KOSPI/KOSDAQ), Pine Screener for custom scanning, global platform with excellent community
- Weaknesses: Custom screener features require paid plan ($14.95+/month), cannot automate local workflows, no programmatic API for screening results, alert limits on free plan

**Investing.com Screener**

**WowNet Pro and Similar Korean Paid Services**

## 4. Scenario Requirements Matrix

### Priority Scenario A2: After-Market Close Daily Screening

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Technical Components** | Data collector (pykrx/FDR), Technical indicator calculator (pandas-ta), Scoring engine (custom Python), Results formatter (Markdown/HTML), Local storage (SQLite) |
| **Data Sources** | pykrx for OHLCV + volume (all KOSPI/KOSDAQ stocks), KRX for stock listings |
| **Computation** | For ~2,500 stocks: calculate MAs (5/20/60/120/200-day), RSI, MACD, ATR, volume averages, RS percentile ranking, VCP detection, base pattern recognition, composite scoring |
| **Output Format** | Ranked table in Markdown (top 20-50 stocks), with columns: Rank, Code, Name, Sector, Score, Sub-scores, Current Price, Volume Ratio, Key Signal |
| **Claude Code Integration** | Python scripts executed via Bash tool; results read and interpreted by Claude for natural-language summary; cron/launchd for scheduling |

### Priority Scenario B1: Individual Stock Technical Deep-Dive

|---|---|
| **Technical Components** | Multi-timeframe data retrieval, comprehensive indicator suite, chart pattern recognition, Claude AI interpretation |
| **Data Sources** | pykrx for daily/weekly OHLCV (single stock, 2+ years history) |
| **Computation** | Full indicator suite for one stock, pattern matching (cup-and-handle, W-bottom, VCP), stage analysis, support/resistance levels |
| **Output Format** | Detailed Markdown report with: Stage classification, key levels, MA alignment status, accumulation assessment, risk/reward analysis, actionable summary |
| **Claude Code Integration** | pykrx-mcp for data retrieval, Python analysis scripts, Claude generates interpretive narrative |

### Priority Scenario C1: Completeness Score Threshold Alert

|---|---|

| **Claude Code Integration** | cron/launchd scheduled execution, macOS notification via `osascript` or terminal-notifier, optional log file |

---

## 5. Branch A vs B Comparison

### Branch A: Claude Code Standalone (No External Tools Beyond Python)

**Fully Serviceable Scenarios:**
- A2 (Daily Screening) — Python scripts + pykrx + pandas-ta, output as Markdown
- A3 (Weekly Summary) — aggregation of daily results
- B1 (Individual Deep-Dive) — pykrx-mcp + Claude interpretation
- B2 (Sector Comparative) — extension of A2 with sector grouping
- B3 (Market Breadth) — computable from the same data
- C3 (MA Crossover Alerts) — simple computation
- C4 (RS Ranking Changes) — diff of weekly rankings
- D4 (Export) — CSV/JSON output from Python

**Limitations of Branch A:**
- **No persistent database**: Each run re-fetches or re-reads from flat files; no query optimization
- **No real scheduler**: Claude Code itself does not run cron; the user must set up launchd/cron manually outside Claude Code
- **Data collection speed**: pykrx scraping ~2,500 stocks takes significant time (~30-60 minutes for daily OHLCV of all stocks if fetching individually; much faster if using KRX bulk endpoints)
- **No real-time data**: pykrx provides end-of-day data only
- **No interactive charting**: Text/Markdown output only; no visual charts

### Branch B: External Integration (Database + Scheduler + Specialized Libraries)

**Additionally Serviceable Scenarios:**

**Branch B is necessary** for any scenario beyond basic on-demand analysis. The fundamental requirement of "daily screening of ~2,500 stocks" inherently requires: (1) persistent data storage to avoid re-fetching history every time, (2) a scheduler to automate daily runs, and (3) state tracking for alerts. All of these are lightweight, local, and well-supported on macOS.

### Top 3 Priority Scenarios

**Priority 1: After-Market Close Daily Screening (A2)**
- **Why first**: This is the core value proposition of the entire system. A daily ranked list of stocks sorted by "technical completeness" is the primary deliverable. Every other scenario either feeds into this or extends from it.

**Priority 2: Individual Stock Technical Deep-Dive (B1)**
- **Why second**: Once the daily screen produces candidates, the user needs to drill into individual stocks for confirmation before making trading decisions. This is the natural "second step" in the workflow.
- **Feasibility**: High. Leverages the same data infrastructure as A2. Claude Code's natural language capabilities add significant value in generating interpretive reports.
- **Differentiation**: No existing tool provides AI-generated natural-language technical analysis of Korean stocks in this integrated manner.

**Priority 3: Completeness Score Threshold Alert (C1)**
- **Why third**: Transforms the system from pull-based (user must remember to run it) to push-based (system alerts the user). This is where automation provides the most time savings.
- **Feasibility**: Medium. Requires launchd scheduling, persistent score history in SQLite, and macOS notification integration. All technically straightforward but adds operational complexity.

### Core Components Required by All Priority Scenarios

1. **Data Collection Layer**: pykrx-based Python scripts for OHLCV data of all KOSPI/KOSDAQ stocks
2. **Local Database**: SQLite database storing historical OHLCV data and computed scores
3. **Technical Indicator Engine**: pandas-ta for MA, RSI, MACD, ATR, Bollinger Bands, volume analysis

6. **Output Formatter**: Markdown table generation for Claude Code consumption
7. **MCP Integration**: pykrx-mcp (or custom MCP server) for interactive Claude Code queries

# KOSPI/KOSDAQ Stock Technical Completeness Analysis & Selection System: Complete Scenario Exploration

## 1. Defining "Technical Completeness" (기술적 완성도)

### 1.1 What the Term Means

"Technical completeness" (기술적 완성도) is **not a formally standardized term** in Korean financial literature. There is no single canonical definition, no published scoring rubric, and no widely-cited academic paper defining it as a discrete metric. Rather, it is a **composite concept** used by Korean retail traders and stock community participants (e.g., on Daum Cafe "부자아빠 주식학교," Naver stock forums) to describe **how "ready" a stock's chart is for a major breakout move**.

The concept synthesizes several well-known Western and Korean technical analysis frameworks:

### 1.2 Component Concepts

**A. Base Formation Quality (바닥 다지기 / 베이스 완성)**
- Prolonged sideways consolidation after a decline
- The longer and tighter the base, the higher the "completeness"
- Equivalent to Stan Weinstein's Stage 1 (Basing) and William O'Neil's base patterns
- Korean traders look for: the stock no longer making new lows, moving average lines converging/flattening

**B. Accumulation Phase Completion (매집 완성도)**
- Evidence that institutional or "force" (세력) players have accumulated shares
- Signals: gradually increasing volume on up-days, decreasing volume on down-days
- The "매집 완성" signal: volume dries up completely on pullbacks (supply exhaustion), followed by a sudden volume surge (2026 example: DL E&C showed quiet accumulation from Jan-Mar 2026, then exploded on March 20 with massive volume)
- Price volatility narrows progressively (the VCP concept)

**C. Moving Average Alignment (이평선 정배열)**
- "정배열" (positive alignment) means: current price > short-term MA > mid-term MA > long-term MA, ordered top-to-bottom
- This indicates a confirmed uptrend structure
- Key MAs used in Korean markets: 5-day, 20-day, 60-day, 120-day, 200-day (or 240-day for trading days)
- The transition from 역배열 (reverse/negative alignment) through convergence to 정배열 is a key "completeness" progression

**D. Breakout Readiness (돌파 준비)**
- The stock is at or near a clearly defined resistance level (pivot point)
- Volume is contracting (calm before the storm)
- Price range is tightening (Volatility Contraction Pattern / VCP)
- The stock is "one catalyst away" from a breakout

### 1.3 Closest Western Equivalents

| Korean Concept | Western Framework | Key Proponent |
|---|---|---|
| 기술적 완성도 (overall) | SEPA Trend Template + VCP | Mark Minervini |
| 바닥 다지기 | Stage 1 Basing | Stan Weinstein |
| 매집 완성도 | Accumulation/Distribution | Wyckoff Method |
| 이평선 정배열 | Moving Average Alignment | General TA |
| 돌파 준비 | Cup-with-Handle pivot, VCP breakout | William O'Neil, Minervini |
| 상대 강도 | Relative Strength Rating | IBD (Investor's Business Daily) |

### 1.4 Proposed Scoring Methodology

Since no standard scoring exists, the system must **construct** one. Based on the research, the most rigorous approach combines:

1. **Minervini Trend Template (8-point checklist)**: Binary pass/fail on whether a stock is in a Stage 2 uptrend
2. **Base Pattern Quality Score**: Depth of correction (shallower = better), duration (adequate time = better), number of VCP contractions (more = better), volume behavior
3. **Moving Average Alignment Score**: Degree of 정배열, slope of key MAs, price distance from MAs
4. **Relative Strength Percentile**: IBD-style RS rating adapted to KOSPI/KOSDAQ universe (weighted 12-month price performance percentile)
5. **Volume Behavior Score**: Accumulation/distribution ratio, volume trend during consolidation, dry-up quality
6. **Breakout Proximity**: How close the stock is to its pivot point / resistance level

**Composite "Technical Completeness Score"** = weighted sum of the above, normalized to 0-100.

### 1.5 Key References for Korean Traders
- Mark Minervini, "Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard" and "Think and Trade Like a Champion"
- William O'Neil, "How to Make Money in Stocks" (CANSLIM)
- Stan Weinstein, "Secrets for Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets"
- Korean community resources: Daum Cafe "부자아빠 주식학교," Naver stock communities
- "상승하는 차트의 조건과 차트의 기본기" by 고짹짹 (Korean chart analysis guide)

---

## 2. Scenario Landscape Map

### Category A: Daily Screening Workflows

| Scenario | Frequency | Complexity | Data Requirements | Automation Potential | Value Delivered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A1: Morning Pre-Market Scan** | Daily (before 9:00 AM KST) | Medium | Previous day's OHLCV, overnight news sentiment | High — fully automatable with scheduled script | Saves 30-60 min of manual chart review; catches overnight developments |
| **A2: After-Market Close Screening** | Daily (after 3:30 PM KST) | Medium | Today's OHLCV + volume, updated technical indicators | High — fully automatable | Most critical workflow; the primary use case. Produces daily "watch list" |
| **A3: Weekly Summary & Sector Rotation** | Weekly (weekend) | Medium-High | 5-day aggregated data, sector indices, breadth data | High — fully automatable | Identifies sector rotation trends, weekly RS leaders; saves 2-3 hours |
| **A4: Monthly Portfolio Rebalancing Signals** | Monthly | High | 20+ trading days data, fundamental overlays desirable | Partial — scoring automated, rebalancing decision needs human | Systematic review; prevents holding deteriorating positions |

### Category B: Deep Analysis Workflows

| **B1: Individual Stock Technical Deep-Dive** | On-demand | High | Multi-timeframe OHLCV (daily/weekly/monthly), historical patterns | Partial — computation automated, interpretation needs Claude AI | Replaces manual chart reading; provides structured analysis report |
| **B2: Sector/Industry Comparative Analysis** | Weekly-Monthly | High | All stocks within sector, sector index, relative performance | High — fully automatable ranking/scoring | Identifies strongest stocks within strongest sectors |
| **B3: Market Breadth & Technical Health** | Daily-Weekly | Medium | Advance/decline data, new highs/lows, % above MAs | High — fully automatable | Market timing context; avoids buying in weak markets |
| **B4: Historical Pattern Backtesting** | Ad-hoc | Very High | Years of historical data, pattern recognition engine | Medium — computation automated, strategy design needs human | Validates that the scoring system actually predicts outcomes |

### Category C: Alert/Monitoring Workflows

| Scenario | Frequency | Complexity | Data Requirements | Automation Potential | Value Delivered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **C1: Completeness Score Threshold Alert** | Continuous/Daily | Medium | Updated scores, configurable thresholds | High — fully automatable with cron/launchd | The "notification" version of A2; push-based rather than pull-based |
| **C2: Volume Spike Detection** | Daily | Low-Medium | Daily volume vs. historical average | High | Early warning of 세력 activity; time-sensitive |
| **C3: Moving Average Crossover Alerts** | Daily | Low | MA calculations | High | Classic signal detection; widely understood |
| **C4: Relative Strength Ranking Changes** | Weekly | Medium | Full universe RS calculation | High | Catches momentum shifts before breakout |

### Category D: Custom/Advanced Workflows

| Scenario | Frequency | Complexity | Data Requirements | Automation Potential | Value Delivered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **D1: Custom Indicator Development** | Ad-hoc | Very High | Raw OHLCV, Python dev environment | Low — inherently creative/experimental | Enables power users to extend the system |
| **D2: Multi-Timeframe Analysis** | Daily-Weekly | High | Daily, weekly, monthly OHLCV (same stock) | High — computation automated | Provides confirmation across timeframes; reduces false signals |
| **D3: Correlation/Pair Analysis** | Ad-hoc | High | Multiple stock series, statistical computation | Medium | Portfolio diversification; pairs trading opportunities |
| **D4: Export to External Tools** | On-demand | Low-Medium | Computed scores and data | High | CSV/Excel/Google Sheets integration; bridges to brokerage tools |

---

## 3. Alternative Tools & Methods Investigation

### Category A: Korean Brokerage Built-in Screeners

**Kiwoom Securities HeroesWorld (키움증권 영웅문 조건검색)**
- Strengths: Real-time data, direct order execution integration, up to 20 combinable indicators (technical + fundamental + pattern + ranking), "조건검색시그널" for real-time alerts, and "영웅검색" AI-powered search
- Weaknesses: (1) System capacity limits during volatile markets — orders can be omitted/delayed. (2) Maximum 20 indicator combinations. (3) Based only on KRX market data. (4) Real-time indicator conditions may return zero results. (5) Windows-only HTS. (6) Cannot implement custom composite scoring. (7) No export API for programmatic use of results
- Cost: Free with brokerage account
- Local execution: Windows only (HTS); mobile app available
- Relationship to our system: **COMPLEMENT** — Kiwoom excels at real-time order execution but cannot implement the custom "technical completeness" scoring methodology. Our system provides the scoring/analysis layer; Kiwoom provides the execution layer

**Samsung Securities POP (삼성증권), NH Investment (NH투자증권 나무), Mirae Asset (미래에셋증권)**
- All provide similar condition-search capabilities
- Samsung offers POP HTS (general) and POP DTS (professional)
- NH offers automated RP purchase; Mirae Asset is known for fast response
- None offer REST API; Korea Investment & Securities (한국투자증권) is the **only** Korean brokerage offering a public REST API
- Relationship: **COMPLEMENT** for the same reasons as Kiwoom

### Category B: Korean Financial Data Platforms

**Naver Finance (네이버 증권)**
- Strengths: Free, comprehensive coverage of all KOSPI/KOSDAQ stocks, real-time quotes, basic screening filters, widely used
- Weaknesses: No custom scoring, limited technical indicator combinations, no API (web scraping needed and fragile), no export, no automation
- Cost: Free
- Relationship: **Our system REPLACES Naver's basic screening** while using Naver as a potential data source (via pykrx's Naver scraping)

**Hankyung Screener (한경닷컴 스크리너) and FnGuide Screener**
- Strengths: Professional-grade fundamental screening, customizable filters
- Weaknesses: Primarily fundamental, not technical-analysis-focused; web-only, no API
- Cost: Free (basic) / Paid (premium features)
- Relationship: **COMPLEMENT** — these focus on fundamentals, our system focuses on technicals

**KRX Data Marketplace (한국거래소 데이터 마켓플레이스)**
- Strengths: Official exchange data, comprehensive (OHLCV, indices, short selling, investor breakdown, ETF), KRX Open API available
- Weaknesses: API call limit of 10,000/day, requires registration, raw data only (no analysis)
- Cost: Free (with registration)
- Relationship: **DATA SOURCE** — potentially a primary data source for our system

### Category C: Python-Based Open Source Tools

**pykrx (sharebook-kr/pykrx)**
- Strengths: KRX + Naver data scraping, KOSPI/KOSDAQ/KONEX support, OHLCV + financial statements + investor supply/demand + short selling data, adjusted/unadjusted prices, Python-native
- Weaknesses: Scraping-based (fragile if source HTML changes), ~4 hours for 3 years of all-stock data, ~1 min per stock for 20 years, no built-in technical indicators
- Cost: Free (MIT license)
- Local execution: Fully local
- Relationship: **PRIMARY DATA COLLECTION LAYER** for our system

**pykrx-mcp (sharebook-kr/pykrx-mcp)**
- Strengths: MCP server wrapping pykrx, directly usable from Claude Desktop/Claude Code, natural language queries for stock data
- Weaknesses: Inherits pykrx's speed limitations, MCP overhead, no batch processing optimization for 2,500 stocks
- Cost: Free (MIT license)
- Relationship: **CRITICAL INTEGRATION POINT** — this is the bridge between Claude Code and Korean stock data

**FinanceDataReader (FDR)**
- Strengths: Multi-source (Yahoo, Naver, KRX), global coverage, both adjusted and unadjusted prices, easy API
- Weaknesses: Yahoo source can be unreliable for Korean stocks, no investor supply/demand data, no short selling data
- Cost: Free
- Relationship: **ALTERNATIVE/BACKUP data layer** — pykrx is more comprehensive for Korean-specific data

**Technical Indicator Libraries**
- **TA-Lib**: 150+ indicators, C-based (fast), well-established; requires compilation on macOS
- **pandas-ta**: 130+ indicators, pure Python, easier installation, Pandas-native
- **ta (Technical Analysis Library in Python)**: Clean documentation, Pandas-native
- Relationship: **CORE COMPUTATION LAYER** — pandas-ta is recommended for ease of installation on macOS

**Existing GitHub Projects**
- **hyunyulhenry/quant_py**: Korean quant investing cookbook; good reference for data collection patterns
- **koreainvestment/open-trading-api**: Korea Investment Securities official samples with LLM integration
- **E-know/AutoKStock**: Auto-trading system
- **KORStockScan**: AI-based KOSPI quant auto-trading with Kiwoom REST API
- Relationship: **REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATIONS** — none fully implement "technical completeness" scoring

**Korean Stock MCP Servers (already existing)**
- **jjlabsio/korea-stock-mcp**: DART + KRX integration, financial statements, daily trading info
- **Mrbaeksang/korea-stock-analyzer-mcp**: 6 investment guru strategies (Buffett, Lynch, Graham, Greenblatt, Fisher, Templeton), PER/PBR/EPS/ROE + MA/RSI/MACD
- Relationship: **COMPLEMENT/EXTEND** — Mrbaeksang's MCP has basic technical indicators but not the full completeness scoring methodology. Could be a foundation to build upon

### Category D: Commercial Tools

**TradingView**
- Strengths: Best-in-class charting, Pine Script for custom indicators, built-in screener for Korean stocks (KOSPI/KOSDAQ), Pine Screener for custom scanning, global platform with excellent community
- Weaknesses: Custom screener features require paid plan ($14.95+/month), cannot automate local workflows, no programmatic API for screening results, alert limits on free plan
- Cost: Free (basic) / $14.95-$59.95/month (pro features)
- Local execution: Cloud-based (web)
- Relationship: **Our system REPLACES TradingView screening** for the specific "technical completeness" use case, while TradingView remains superior for interactive charting and visual confirmation

**Investing.com Screener**
- Strengths: Comprehensive, supports Korean stocks
- Weaknesses: Advanced filters require Pro+ subscription, web-only
- Cost: Free (basic) / Paid (Pro+)
- Relationship: **REPLACEABLE** by our system for technical screening

**WowNet Pro and Similar Korean Paid Services**
- Strengths: Korean-market-specific, professional tools
- Weaknesses: Subscription cost, cannot customize scoring algorithm
- Relationship: **REPLACEABLE** for technical completeness scoring

---

## 4. Scenario Requirements Matrix

### Priority Scenario A2: After-Market Close Daily Screening

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Technical Components** | Data collector (pykrx/FDR), Technical indicator calculator (pandas-ta), Scoring engine (custom Python), Results formatter (Markdown/HTML), Local storage (SQLite) |
| **Data Sources** | pykrx for OHLCV + volume (all KOSPI/KOSDAQ stocks), KRX for stock listings |
| **Computation** | For ~2,500 stocks: calculate MAs (5/20/60/120/200-day), RSI, MACD, ATR, volume averages, RS percentile ranking, VCP detection, base pattern recognition, composite scoring |
| **Output Format** | Ranked table in Markdown (top 20-50 stocks), with columns: Rank, Code, Name, Sector, Score, Sub-scores, Current Price, Volume Ratio, Key Signal |
| **Claude Code Integration** | Python scripts executed via Bash tool; results read and interpreted by Claude for natural-language summary; cron/launchd for scheduling |

### Priority Scenario B1: Individual Stock Technical Deep-Dive

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Technical Components** | Multi-timeframe data retrieval, comprehensive indicator suite, chart pattern recognition, Claude AI interpretation |
| **Data Sources** | pykrx for daily/weekly OHLCV (single stock, 2+ years history) |
| **Computation** | Full indicator suite for one stock, pattern matching (cup-and-handle, W-bottom, VCP), stage analysis, support/resistance levels |
| **Output Format** | Detailed Markdown report with: Stage classification, key levels, MA alignment status, accumulation assessment, risk/reward analysis, actionable summary |
| **Claude Code Integration** | pykrx-mcp for data retrieval, Python analysis scripts, Claude generates interpretive narrative |

### Priority Scenario C1: Completeness Score Threshold Alert

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Technical Components** | Same as A2 plus threshold configuration, change detection, notification system |
| **Data Sources** | Same as A2 |
| **Computation** | Same as A2 plus: compare today's scores with yesterday's, detect threshold crossings, detect significant score changes |
| **Output Format** | Short alert message (stock code, name, old score, new score, trigger reason) |
| **Claude Code Integration** | cron/launchd scheduled execution, macOS notification via `osascript` or terminal-notifier, optional log file |

---

## 5. Branch A vs B Comparison

### Branch A: Claude Code Standalone (No External Tools Beyond Python)

**Fully Serviceable Scenarios:**
- A2 (Daily Screening) — Python scripts + pykrx + pandas-ta, output as Markdown
- A3 (Weekly Summary) — aggregation of daily results
- B1 (Individual Deep-Dive) — pykrx-mcp + Claude interpretation
- B2 (Sector Comparative) — extension of A2 with sector grouping
- B3 (Market Breadth) — computable from the same data
- C3 (MA Crossover Alerts) — simple computation
- C4 (RS Ranking Changes) — diff of weekly rankings
- D4 (Export) — CSV/JSON output from Python

**Limitations of Branch A:**
- **No persistent database**: Each run re-fetches or re-reads from flat files; no query optimization
- **No real scheduler**: Claude Code itself does not run cron; the user must set up launchd/cron manually outside Claude Code
- **Data collection speed**: pykrx scraping ~2,500 stocks takes significant time (~30-60 minutes for daily OHLCV of all stocks if fetching individually; much faster if using KRX bulk endpoints)
- **No real-time data**: pykrx provides end-of-day data only
- **No interactive charting**: Text/Markdown output only; no visual charts

### Branch B: External Integration (Database + Scheduler + Specialized Libraries)

**Additionally Serviceable Scenarios:**
- A1 (Pre-Market Scan) — requires launchd/cron scheduling + potentially real-time data via Korea Investment Securities REST API
- A4 (Monthly Rebalancing) — benefits from SQLite historical score tracking
- B4 (Backtesting) — requires historical database, vectorized computation
- C1 (Threshold Alerts) — requires persistent state (yesterday's scores) + scheduler + notification
- C2 (Volume Spike) — requires reliable scheduled execution + notification
- D1 (Custom Indicators) — benefits from a structured data layer
- D2 (Multi-Timeframe) — benefits from pre-stored weekly/monthly data in SQLite
- D3 (Correlation) — requires historical database

**Branch B Components:**
| Component | Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Database | SQLite | Local, zero-config, file-based; stores OHLCV history + computed scores |
| Scheduler | macOS launchd (or cron) | Triggers daily/weekly data collection and analysis runs |
| Data Collector | pykrx + custom Python scripts | Incremental daily data fetching (~5-10 min for daily delta of all stocks) |
| Indicator Engine | pandas-ta or TA-Lib | Compute 10+ technical indicators per stock |
| Scoring Engine | Custom Python | Composite technical completeness scoring |
| MCP Server | pykrx-mcp (extended) or custom | Bridges Claude Code to the data/analysis layer |
| Notification | terminal-notifier or osascript | macOS native notifications for alerts |
| Export | Python csv/openpyxl | CSV/Excel output |

### Verdict

**Branch B is necessary** for any scenario beyond basic on-demand analysis. The fundamental requirement of "daily screening of ~2,500 stocks" inherently requires: (1) persistent data storage to avoid re-fetching history every time, (2) a scheduler to automate daily runs, and (3) state tracking for alerts. All of these are lightweight, local, and well-supported on macOS.

---

## 6. Final Conclusions

### Top 3 Priority Scenarios

**Priority 1: After-Market Close Daily Screening (A2)**
- **Why first**: This is the core value proposition of the entire system. A daily ranked list of stocks sorted by "technical completeness" is the primary deliverable. Every other scenario either feeds into this or extends from it.
- **Feasibility**: High. All required components exist: pykrx for data, pandas-ta for indicators, Python for scoring, SQLite for persistence, launchd for scheduling.
- **Implementation estimate**: The data collection pipeline + scoring engine + output formatter represent the system's foundation.

**Priority 2: Individual Stock Technical Deep-Dive (B1)**
- **Why second**: Once the daily screen produces candidates, the user needs to drill into individual stocks for confirmation before making trading decisions. This is the natural "second step" in the workflow.
- **Feasibility**: High. Leverages the same data infrastructure as A2. Claude Code's natural language capabilities add significant value in generating interpretive reports.
- **Differentiation**: No existing tool provides AI-generated natural-language technical analysis of Korean stocks in this integrated manner.

**Priority 3: Completeness Score Threshold Alert (C1)**
- **Why third**: Transforms the system from pull-based (user must remember to run it) to push-based (system alerts the user). This is where automation provides the most time savings.
- **Feasibility**: Medium. Requires launchd scheduling, persistent score history in SQLite, and macOS notification integration. All technically straightforward but adds operational complexity.

### Core Components Required by All Priority Scenarios

1. **Data Collection Layer**: pykrx-based Python scripts for OHLCV data of all KOSPI/KOSDAQ stocks
2. **Local Database**: SQLite database storing historical OHLCV data and computed scores
3. **Technical Indicator Engine**: pandas-ta for MA, RSI, MACD, ATR, Bollinger Bands, volume analysis
4. **Scoring Engine**: Custom Python implementing the "Technical Completeness Score" (TCS) composite metric
5. **Relative Strength Calculator**: IBD-style RS percentile ranking across the full KOSPI/KOSDAQ universe
6. **Output Formatter**: Markdown table generation for Claude Code consumption
7. **MCP Integration**: pykrx-mcp (or custom MCP server) for interactive Claude Code queries

### Deferred Scenarios

| Scenario | Trigger to Revisit |
|---|---|
| A1 (Pre-Market Scan) | After A2 is stable for 2+ weeks; user requests real-time capability |
| A4 (Monthly Rebalancing) | After accumulating 1+ month of daily score history |
| B3 (Market Breadth) | When user wants market timing context; relatively easy to add |
| B4 (Backtesting) | After 3+ months of historical scores accumulated; user wants to validate scoring methodology |
| C2 (Volume Spike) | After C1 is operational; natural extension |
| D2 (Multi-Timeframe) | When user reports false signals from daily-only analysis |
| D4 (Export) | When user explicitly requests Excel/Sheets integration |

### Scenarios This System Should NOT Attempt

1. **Real-time intraday trading signals**: Requires real-time data feeds (brokerage API with WebSocket), sub-second latency, and order execution — this is fundamentally a different system class. Use Kiwoom HTS 조건검색 instead.

2. **Automated order execution**: Even with Korea Investment Securities REST API, automated trading involves regulatory, risk management, and reliability requirements far beyond a screening tool. Use dedicated auto-trading platforms.

3. **Fundamental analysis scoring**: While useful as a supplement, comprehensive fundamental analysis (재무제표 분석, PER/PBR/ROE scoring) is a separate domain. Use Mrbaeksang's korea-stock-analyzer-mcp or FnGuide for this.

4. **News sentiment analysis**: While theoretically valuable, Korean financial news NLP is a massive separate project. TradingView and commercial tools already handle this.

5. **Interactive charting**: Building a chart rendering engine is enormous effort for marginal gain. Use TradingView for visual chart confirmation after the system identifies candidates.

---

## Parking Lot

| # | Discovery | Source Branch | Follow-up Category |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | pykrx-mcp already exists as an MCP server for Claude — could be extended rather than building from scratch | Alternative Tools (3C) | Technical |
| P2 | korea-stock-analyzer-mcp (Mrbaeksang) provides basic technical indicators (MA, RSI, MACD) + fundamental data — could serve as a complementary MCP | Alternative Tools (3C) | External Integration |
| P3 | KRX Open API has 10,000 calls/day limit; pykrx scraping is not rate-limited but slow (~4 hours for 3 years of all stocks). Incremental daily updates would be fast (~5-10 min) | Data Requirements (4) | Technical |
| P4 | Korea Investment Securities is the ONLY Korean brokerage with a public REST API — this is the sole path to real-time data and order execution if ever needed | Alternative Tools (3A) | External Integration |
| P5 | No existing tool/project implements a "technical completeness" composite score for Korean stocks — this is genuinely novel, meaning no reference implementation exists to validate against | Definition (1) | Structural Risk |
| P6 | pandas-ta is recommended over TA-Lib for macOS due to easier installation (no C compilation needed) | Technical Stack (4) | Technical |
| P7 | SQLite is the natural choice for local storage — zero-config, file-based, excellent Python support, adequate for ~2,500 stocks x 5 years of daily data (~3M rows) | Architecture (4) | Technical |
| P8 | macOS launchd is preferred over cron for scheduling on modern macOS (cron is deprecated); `launchctl` provides better system integration | Architecture (4) | Technical |
| P9 | The scoring methodology itself is an intellectual/creative design task, not an engineering task — it requires domain expertise in Korean stock trading and will likely need iterative refinement based on backtesting results | Definition (1) | User Behavior |
| P10 | TradingView's Pine Screener could potentially be used as a validation benchmark — run the same logic in Pine Script and compare results | Alternative Tools (3D) | External Integration |
| P11 | VCP pattern detection is algorithmically complex (requires identifying successive contractions with decreasing amplitude) — this may be the hardest single component to implement | Scoring Methodology (1) | Technical |
| P12 | The IBD RS Rating formula (40% most recent quarter + 20% each of prior 3 quarters) is well-documented and directly implementable for the Korean market | Scoring Methodology (1) | Technical |

---

input.prompt:
You are the **Operator Analyst** investigating user experience, operational friction, and practical usability for a system called "KOSPI/KOSDAQ Stock Technical Completeness Analysis & Selection System" (KOSPI·KOSDAQ 종목 기술적 완성도 분석 및 선별 시스템).

This system will run ENTIRELY on the user's LOCAL macOS computer as an AI agentic workflow automation built on Claude Code. The system:
1. Collects stock data for all KOSPI and KOSDAQ listed companies (~2,500 stocks)
2. Analyzes "technical completeness" (기술적 완성도) — technical analysis indicators showing chart pattern maturity, base formation completion, moving average alignment, breakout readiness
3. Filters/selects stocks meeting criteria
4. Presents results to the user

**CRITICAL CONSTRAINT**: This system runs ONLY on the user's local macOS machine. No SaaS, no cloud hosting.

**KEY CONTEXT**: The user (who commissioned this system) has stated they "don't know how to build this system at all" (이 시스템을 어떻게 만들지 전혀 모른다). This is a critical design constraint.

## Your Investigation: TWO User Profiles

### Branch A: Power User (파워 유저 — 복잡한 멀티에이전트 설계자)

Persona: A technically skilled Claude Code Max subscriber who designs multi-agent workflows, comfortable with terminal, Python, and configuration files.

**1. Persona Detail**
- Background: Software developer or technical trader with Python experience
- Current workflow: Uses TradingView + manual chart review + maybe some basic Python scripts
- Core frustration: Repetitive manual work screening 2,500 stocks daily
- Expectation: Full control, customizable scoring, transparent computation

**2. Components This User Needs**
- MUST HAVE (without these, they won't use this system):
  - Customizable scoring parameters (weights, thresholds)
  - Direct access to raw data and intermediate results
  - Ability to modify/extend analysis scripts
- NICE TO HAVE:
  - Pipeline monitoring/observability
  - Version control of configuration changes
  - Performance benchmarking tools

**3. Acceptable Complexity Level**
- Willing to invest: 2-4 hours in initial setup
- CLAUDE.md direct editing: Yes, comfortable
- Terminal commands for setup: Expected
- Debugging enthusiasm: High — wants to understand the internals
- Configuration complexity tolerance: High

**4. User Journey**
Map the power user's journey:
- Installation: `git clone` → `pip install` → configure → test run
- First use: Run full scan, examine results, adjust parameters
- Daily use: Quick `/scan` command, review top candidates
- Customization: Modify scoring weights, add new indicators
- Advanced: Build custom screeners, backtest strategies

**5. Friction Points for Power User**
- What could make them abandon this system?
- What could make them prefer building from scratch instead?
- What's the minimum quality threshold for results?

### Branch B: General User (일반 사용자 — 단순 자동화 사용자)

Persona: A Claude Code subscriber who trades Korean stocks but has LIMITED technical skills. They want results, not infrastructure. **This matches the actual user profile** based on the user's self-description.

**1. Persona Detail**
- Background: Individual stock trader, may use HTS (키움증권 영웅문 etc.), NOT a programmer
- Current workflow: Manual chart review on Naver Finance / TradingView / HTS, reads stock community posts
- Core frustration: Can't review 2,500 stocks manually; misses opportunities; no systematic approach
- Expectation: "Give me a list of stocks ready to break out. I'll do the final chart check myself."

**2. Components This User Needs**
- MUST HAVE (without these, they won't use this system):
  - One-command installation (setup script that just works)
  - Simple daily operation (one slash command to get today's candidates)
  - Clear, understandable output (not raw numbers, but interpreted results)
- NICE TO HAVE:
  - Natural language explanation of WHY each stock is ranked high
  - Comparison with what they see on their brokerage HTS
  - Simple customization (e.g., "I only want KOSDAQ stocks" or "minimum volume 100만주")

**3. Acceptable Complexity Level**
- Willing to invest: 15-30 minutes in initial setup (MAX)
- CLAUDE.md direct editing: Absolutely NOT — they don't know what this is
- Terminal commands: Willing to copy-paste from instructions, but won't debug
- Debugging enthusiasm: Zero — if it breaks, they want to know who to ask
- Configuration complexity tolerance: Very low

**4. User Journey**
Map the general user's journey:
- Installation: Claude Code prompts → "yes" to everything → it works (or they give up)
- First use: Type `/scan` → get a list → open candidates on Naver Finance/HTS for visual confirmation
- Daily use: Open Claude Code → `/scan` → review → done in 5 minutes
- Customization: At most, changing a few parameters via guided prompts
- Troubleshooting: If it breaks, they ask Claude "왜 안 돼?" and expect a fix

**5. Friction Points for General User**
- What could make them abandon this system IMMEDIATELY?
- At what point does setup complexity exceed their patience?
- What error messages would be incomprehensible to them?
- How do you design for "it should just work"?

### Critical Analysis: The Gap Between Branch A and Branch B

**The Installation Problem**
- This system requires: Python 3.10+, pip, virtual environment, pykrx, pandas, pandas-ta, potentially DuckDB/SQLite, launchd configuration
- A power user sets this up in 20 minutes
- A general user may not have Python properly configured, may not know what `pip` is, may have macOS Gatekeeper blocking scripts
- **Question**: Can Claude Code's setup scripts + hooks handle all of this automatically?

**The Daily Operation Problem**
- Power user: Opens terminal, types command, reads output, acts
- General user: Opens Claude Code app, types "오늘 종목 뭐 사?" (what should I buy today?), expects useful response
- **Question**: Can the system bridge this gap with good UX design (slash commands, natural language input)?

**The Error Recovery Problem**
- Power user: Reads error log, fixes the issue, continues
- General user: Sees "pykrx timeout error" and has no idea what to do
- **Question**: Can the system be designed to self-heal common failures (retry, fallback data source, cached results)?

**The Trust Problem**
- Power user: Validates results against their own analysis, adjusts parameters
- General user: Trusts the system's output implicitly OR distrusts it entirely
- **Question**: How to build appropriate trust without requiring the user to understand the methodology?

### Final Comparison (Branch A vs B)

**If we design for Power User first:**
- Design direction: Maximum flexibility, configuration-rich, CLI-first
- Default complexity: High
- General user experience: Terrible (they won't be able to use it)

**If we design for General User first:**
- Design direction: Maximum simplicity, guided experience, sensible defaults
- Default complexity: Low
- Power user experience: Frustrating (they'll hit walls trying to customize)

**Can we serve both?**
- Layered architecture: Simple surface (slash commands) + deep access (config files, scripts)
- Progressive disclosure: Start simple, reveal complexity on demand
- "Zero-config" defaults with "full-config" override capability

**Realistic Questions:**
1. Can we satisfy both user types without doubling the implementation effort?
2. Which user should we prioritize given that the actual user is a general user?
3. What structural changes would be needed later if we start with one user type and add the other?

### 6. Must-Have Components (Prioritized for BOTH Users)

Provide your Top 5 must-have components that serve both user types, ordered by:
1. Criticality (without this, the system is unusable for the target user)
2. Feasibility (can be built with reasonable effort)
3. User impact (delivers the most value per effort)

For each component:
- What it does
- Why it's essential
- Which user type benefits more
- Implementation complexity (low/medium/high)

### 🅿️ Parking Lot
Record findings outside your scope with: discovery, source branch, follow-up category (technical/external-integration/user-behavior/structural-risk)

## Web Research Required
Use WebSearch to find:
1. How other local automation tools (e.g., Shortcuts, Automator, Raycast) handle the "zero-config" installation problem
2. Examples of Claude Code /commands that provide good UX for non-technical users
3. How Korean stock trading tools handle onboarding for non-technical users (키움증권 영웅문 초기 설정 가이드)
4. Claude Code's current capabilities for automated setup (hooks, setup scripts)

Output your full analysis in English, structured with clear headers.

prompt:
You are the **Operator Analyst** investigating user experience, operational friction, and practical usability for a system called "KOSPI/KOSDAQ Stock Technical Completeness Analysis & Selection System" (KOSPI·KOSDAQ 종목 기술적 완성도 분석 및 선별 시스템).

This system will run ENTIRELY on the user's LOCAL macOS computer as an AI agentic workflow automation built on Claude Code. The system:
1. Collects stock data for all KOSPI and KOSDAQ listed companies (~2,500 stocks)
2. Analyzes "technical completeness" (기술적 완성도) — technical analysis indicators showing chart pattern maturity, base formation completion, moving average alignment, breakout readiness
3. Filters/selects stocks meeting criteria
4. Presents results to the user

**CRITICAL CONSTRAINT**: This system runs ONLY on the user's local macOS machine. No SaaS, no cloud hosting.

**KEY CONTEXT**: The user (who commissioned this system) has stated they "don't know how to build this system at all" (이 시스템을 어떻게 만들지 전혀 모른다). This is a critical design constraint.

## Your Investigation: TWO User Profiles

### Branch A: Power User (파워 유저 — 복잡한 멀티에이전트 설계자)

Persona: A technically skilled Claude Code Max subscriber who designs multi-agent workflows, comfortable with terminal, Python, and configuration files.

**1. Persona Detail**
- Background: Software developer or technical trader with Python experience
- Current workflow: Uses TradingView + manual chart review + maybe some basic Python scripts
- Core frustration: Repetitive manual work screening 2,500 stocks daily
- Expectation: Full control, customizable scoring, transparent computation

**2. Components This User Needs**
- MUST HAVE (without these, they won't use this system):
  - Customizable scoring parameters (weights, thresholds)
  - Direct access to raw data and intermediate results
  - Ability to modify/extend analysis scripts
- NICE TO HAVE:
  - Pipeline monitoring/observability
  - Version control of configuration changes
  - Performance benchmarking tools

**3. Acceptable Complexity Level**
- Willing to invest: 2-4 hours in initial setup
- CLAUDE.md direct editing: Yes, comfortable
- Terminal commands for setup: Expected
- Debugging enthusiasm: High — wants to understand the internals
- Configuration complexity tolerance: High

**4. User Journey**
Map the power user's journey:
- Installation: `git clone` → `pip install` → configure → test run
- First use: Run full scan, examine results, adjust parameters
- Daily use: Quick `/scan` command, review top candidates
- Customization: Modify scoring weights, add new indicators
- Advanced: Build custom screeners, backtest strategies

**5. Friction Points for Power User**
- What could make them abandon this system?
- What could make them prefer building from scratch instead?
- What's the minimum quality threshold for results?

### Branch B: General User (일반 사용자 — 단순 자동화 사용자)

Persona: A Claude Code subscriber who trades Korean stocks but has LIMITED technical skills. They want results, not infrastructure. **This matches the actual user profile** based on the user's self-description.

**1. Persona Detail**
- Background: Individual stock trader, may use HTS (키움증권 영웅문 etc.), NOT a programmer
- Current workflow: Manual chart review on Naver Finance / TradingView / HTS, reads stock community posts
- Core frustration: Can't review 2,500 stocks manually; misses opportunities; no systematic approach
- Expectation: "Give me a list of stocks ready to break out. I'll do the final chart check myself."

**2. Components This User Needs**
- MUST HAVE (without these, they won't use this system):
  - One-command installation (setup script that just works)
  - Simple daily operation (one slash command to get today's candidates)
  - Clear, understandable output (not raw numbers, but interpreted results)
- NICE TO HAVE:
  - Natural language explanation of WHY each stock is ranked high
  - Comparison with what they see on their brokerage HTS
  - Simple customization (e.g., "I only want KOSDAQ stocks" or "minimum volume 100만주")

**3. Acceptable Complexity Level**
- Willing to invest: 15-30 minutes in initial setup (MAX)
- CLAUDE.md direct editing: Absolutely NOT — they don't know what this is
- Terminal commands: Willing to copy-paste from instructions, but won't debug
- Debugging enthusiasm: Zero — if it breaks, they want to know who to ask
- Configuration complexity tolerance: Very low

**4. User Journey**
Map the general user's journey:
- Installation: Claude Code prompts → "yes" to everything → it works (or they give up)
- First use: Type `/scan` → get a list → open candidates on Naver Finance/HTS for visual confirmation
- Daily use: Open Claude Code → `/scan` → review → done in 5 minutes
- Customization: At most, changing a few parameters via guided prompts
- Troubleshooting: If it breaks, they ask Claude "왜 안 돼?" and expect a fix

**5. Friction Points for General User**
- What could make them abandon this system IMMEDIATELY?
- At what point does setup complexity exceed their patience?
- What error messages would be incomprehensible to them?
- How do you design for "it should just work"?

### Critical Analysis: The Gap Between Branch A and Branch B

**The Installation Problem**
- This system requires: Python 3.10+, pip, virtual environment, pykrx, pandas, pandas-ta, potentially DuckDB/SQLite, launchd configuration
- A power user sets this up in 20 minutes
- A general user may not have Python properly configured, may not know what `pip` is, may have macOS Gatekeeper blocking scripts
- **Question**: Can Claude Code's setup scripts + hooks handle all of this automatically?

**The Daily Operation Problem**
- Power user: Opens terminal, types command, reads output, acts
- General user: Opens Claude Code app, types "오늘 종목 뭐 사?" (what should I buy today?), expects useful response
- **Question**: Can the system bridge this gap with good UX design (slash commands, natural language input)?

**The Error Recovery Problem**
- Power user: Reads error log, fixes the issue, continues
- General user: Sees "pykrx timeout error" and has no idea what to do
- **Question**: Can the system be designed to self-heal common failures (retry, fallback data source, cached results)?

**The Trust Problem**
- Power user: Validates results against their own analysis, adjusts parameters
- General user: Trusts the system's output implicitly OR distrusts it entirely
- **Question**: How to build appropriate trust without requiring the user to understand the methodology?

### Final Comparison (Branch A vs B)

**If we design for Power User first:**
- Design direction: Maximum flexibility, configuration-rich, CLI-first
- Default complexity: High
- General user experience: Terrible (they won't be able to use it)

**If we design for General User first:**
- Design direction: Maximum simplicity, guided experience, sensible defaults
- Default complexity: Low
- Power user experience: Frustrating (they'll hit walls trying to customize)

**Can we serve both?**
- Layered architecture: Simple surface (slash commands) + deep access (config files, scripts)
- Progressive disclosure: Start simple, reveal complexity on demand
- "Zero-config" defaults with "full-config" override capability

**Realistic Questions:**
1. Can we satisfy both user types without doubling the implementation effort?
2. Which user should we prioritize given that the actual user is a general user?
3. What structural changes would be needed later if we start with one user type and add the other?

### 6. Must-Have Components (Prioritized for BOTH Users)

Provide your Top 5 must-have components that serve both user types, ordered by:
1. Criticality (without this, the system is unusable for the target user)
2. Feasibility (can be built with reasonable effort)
3. User impact (delivers the most value per effort)

For each component:
- What it does
- Why it's essential
- Which user type benefits more
- Implementation complexity (low/medium/high)

### 🅿️ Parking Lot
Record findings outside your scope with: discovery, source branch, follow-up category (technical/external-integration/user-behavior/structural-risk)

## Web Research Required
Use WebSearch to find:
1. How other local automation tools (e.g., Shortcuts, Automator, Raycast) handle the "zero-config" installation problem
2. Examples of Claude Code /commands that provide good UX for non-technical users
3. How Korean stock trading tools handle onboarding for non-technical users (키움증권 영웅문 초기 설정 가이드)
4. Claude Code's current capabilities for automated setup (hooks, setup scripts)

Output your full analysis in English, structured with clear headers.

## Slash Commands and Setup

Slash commands in Claude Code are markdown files placed in .claude/commands/ (project-level) or ~/.claude/commands/ (personal), with the filename becoming the /slash-command. You don't need to memorize the format—just ask Claude to create the slash command for you and it will handle the front matter automatically.

## Accessibility for Non-Technical Users

The most significant development for non-technical users is Claude Cowork (announced January 12, 2026), which will make Claude Code accessible to everyone without the terminal and is currently in research preview for Claude Max subscribers on macOS. Everything you're learning now will apply to an easier interface soon.

## Automation Setup

Custom skills are .md files that give Claude structured workflows for specific tasks, with some team-shared and others personal productivity hacks. If you find yourself giving Claude the same instructions repeatedly, extract them into a skill.

Additionally, MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets Claude talk to external services as native tools, and servers are added in ~/.claude/settings.json.

content.content:
1	# PRD 1차 리서치 - Teammate Execution Framework
2	
3	> **이 문서의 목적**: 가장 넓은 그물을 던지는 1차 광범위 리서치 단계. 이 문서의 산출물은 최종 PRD가 아니라 "1차 PRD 초안 + 후속 심층조사 실행 계획"이다. 이후 기술 심층조사, 외부 연동 심층조사 등 별도의 전문 심층리서치를 거쳐, 모든 결과를 통합한 최종 PRD를 완성한다.
4	
5	## 초기 설정 (당신이 입력할 것)
6	
7	**제품명**: [여기에 입력]
8	**주요 사용 시나리오**: [이 하네스가 자동화할 핵심 작업 유형을 입력]
9	**해결하려는 워크플로우 문제**: [현재 수동으로 하고 있거나 비효율적인 작업 흐름을 입력]
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Fork-Based Sessions Branch Strategy (확장 기능)
14	
15	이 프레임워크는 `/fork` 기능을 활용하여 **각 Phase에서 여러 경로를 동시에 탐색**합니다.
16	이를 통해 더 깊이 있는 리서치, 철저한 토론, 견고한 수렴을 이룹니다.
17	
18	### 전략 개요
19	
20	```
21	초기 설정
22	  ↓
23	[PHASE 1: 조사]
24	  ├─ /fork Branch 1.1: Workflow Architect (가정 A)
25	  ├─ /fork Branch 1.2: Workflow Architect (가정 B)
26	  ├─ /fork Branch 2.1: Scenario Explorer (가정 A)
27	  ├─ /fork Branch 2.2: Scenario Explorer (가정 B)
28	  ├─ /fork Branch 3.1: Operator Analyst (가정 A)
29	  ├─ /fork Branch 3.2: Operator Analyst (가정 B)
30	  ├─ /fork Branch 4.1: Sustainability Strategist (가정 A)
31	  └─ /fork Branch 4.2: Sustainability Strategist (가정 B)
32	  ↓
33	[PHASE 2: 토론]
34	  ├─ /fork Branch 2.A: 워크플로우 구조 우선 토론
35	  ├─ /fork Branch 2.B: 사용 시나리오 커버리지 우선 토론
36	  ├─ /fork Branch 2.C: 운용성/사용자 경험 우선 토론
37	  └─ /fork Branch 2.D: 지속 가능성/효율 우선 토론
38	  ↓
39	[PHASE 3: 수렴]
40	  ├─ /fork Branch 3.A: Deep Automation (고도 자동화)
41	  ├─ /fork Branch 3.B: Selective Automation (선택적 자동화)
42	  └─ /fork Branch 3.C: Minimal Automation (최소 자동화)
43	  ↓
44	[PHASE 4: 통합]
45	  → 3개 시나리오 비교
46	  → 1차 PRD 초안 확정
47	  → 후속 심층조사 실행 계획 산출
48	```
49	
50	### Branch 사용의 목적
51	
52	**조사 Phase에서의 Branch**
53	- 같은 관점에서도 다양한 가정이 가능함을 인정
54	- 각 가정이 타당한 근거를 가질 수 있음을 검증
55	- 탐색 중 범위 밖 발견은 파킹 로트에 포착
56	
57	**가정 축 설정 지침**: 프로젝트 시작 시 다음 후보 중에서 가장 의미 있는 1개를 선택한다.
58	- "Claude Code 단독 완결 vs 외부 도구 연동 전제"
59	- "단일 사용자 전용 vs 팀 공유 가능 구조"
60	- "단일 프로젝트 집중 vs 멀티 프로젝트 동시 관리"
61	- "최소 자동화(사용자 개입 많음) vs 최대 자동화(완전 자율 실행)"
62	
63	어떤 축을 선택하든 2개의 대립 가정을 강제로 탐색하게 되어 그물의 넓이가 보장된다.
64	
65	**토론 Phase에서의 Branch**
66	- 어떤 관점을 가장 우선시하냐에 따라 결론이 달라짐을 검증
67	- "워크플로우 구조 우선" vs "시나리오 커버리지 우선" vs "운용성 우선" vs "지속 가능성 우선"의 각 경로가 다른 PRD를 만듦
68	- 각 경로의 장단점 파악
69	
70	**수렴 Phase에서의 Branch**
71	- 자동화 범위와 구조적 복잡도를 기준으로 3가지 시나리오 동시 검증
72	- "만약 우리가 더 고도로 자동화했다면?" "더 최소한으로 시작했다면?"을 동시에 평가
73	- 각 시나리오가 4개 카테고리의 후속 조사 항목을 출력하여 심층조사 단계와 연결
74	
75	---
76	
77	## 실행 제약 (Constraints)
78	
79	이 프로세스를 진행할 때 다음 제약을 유지하세요:
80	
81	**조사 단계 제약**
82	- 각 Teammate는 **근거 없는 주장 금지** (추측/직관만으로는 안 됨)
83	- 대안 워크플로우 도구·방법론을 조사할 때는 해당 도구가 실제로 로컬 환경에서 작동하는지 **실행 가능성을 확인**해야 함
84	- Claude Code의 실제 실행 한계(컨텍스트 윈도우 크기, 토큰 소비 속도, 병렬 Teammate 수 제한, Hooks의 조건 분기 지원 범위)를 **반드시 명시**해야 함
85	- "불가능하다"는 결론을 낼 때는 **기술적 제약의 구체적 지점**(어떤 API가 없는지, 어떤 기능이 미지원인지)을 명시해야 함
86	- 각 Teammate는 다른 관점의 영향을 받지 말 것 (독립성 유지)
87	- **파킹 로트 규칙**: 조사 중 발견했으나 현재 Branch의 관점이나 범위를 넘는 사항은 파킹 로트에 기록한다. 발견 내용, 발견한 Branch, 해당하는 후속 조사 카테고리(기술/외부연동/사용자행동/구조적리스크)를 명시한다.
88	
89	**토론 단계 제약**
90	- Moderator는 중립 입장 유지 (특정 팀의 편 들지 않기)
91	- 한 관점이 연속 3번 이상 강조하면, 반대 관점에 명시적 발언 기회 제공
92	- "동의한다"만으로는 안 됨 → "왜 동의하는가" 근거 포함 필수
93	- 충돌이 없으면 안 됨 (4개 관점이 모두 일치하면 토론 깊이가 부족한 신호)
94	- **파킹 로트 규칙**: 토론 중 발견된 범위 밖 사항도 동일하게 파킹 로트에 기록한다.
95	
96	**수렴 단계 제약**
97	- Green Zone: **4개 관점 모두 동의** (3개만 동의하면 Yellow Zone)
98	- Yellow Zone: **명확한 트리거 조건** 정의 필수 ("언제 포함될 것인가?")
99	- Red Zone: **재검토 시점 명시** ("6개월 후" 또는 "~이면 검토")
100	- 구성 요소는 최대 15개 이내로 집약 (산만해지면 안 됨)

description: Reading prompt/prd_teammate_executable.md

content.content:
100	- 구성 요소는 최대 15개 이내로 집약 (산만해지면 안 됨)
101	- **각 시나리오는 반드시 4개 카테고리의 후속 조사 항목을 출력**해야 함
102	
103	---
104	
105	## 성공 지표 (Success Points)
106	
107	이 리서치 프로세스가 **성공했는지** 판단하는 기준:
108	
109	### Phase 1 (조사) 성공 지표
110	✅ **각 Teammate별 결론이 구체적인가?**
111	- [ ] 워크플로우 구성 요소(Hook, Teammate, Pipeline, Trigger 등)가 구체적인가 (예: "자동화" ❌ → "커밋 시 자동 린트 + 테스트 실행 Hook" ✅)
112	- [ ] 근거가 명시되어 있는가 (예: "Claude Code Hooks 공식 문서 기준...", "실제 실행 테스트 결과...")
113	- [ ] 우선순위가 명확한가 (Top 3이 명확히 도출됨)
114	
115	✅ **4개 관점이 서로 다른 각도에서 봤는가?**
116	- [ ] Workflow Architect만 강조하는 구성 요소가 있는가? (파이프라인 구조만 보는 것)
117	- [ ] Scenario Explorer만 강조하는 시나리오가 있는가? (커버리지만 보는 것)
118	- [ ] Operator Analyst만 조심하는 마찰 지점이 있는가? (사용성 문제)
119	- [ ] Sustainability Strategist가 우려하는 구조적 한계가 있는가? (지속 가능성 문제)
120	- → 모두 있으면 ✅ 다각적 분석 성공
121	
122	### Phase 2 (토론) 성공 지표
123	✅ **충돌이 명확히 드러났는가?**
124	- [ ] 최소 3개 이상의 의견 불일치 포착됨
125	- [ ] 각 불일치마다 "왜 다른가"의 근거가 명시됨
126	- [ ] 단순 선호도 차이가 아니라 **논리적 충돌**임
127	
128	✅ **합의 영역이 명확해졌는가?**
129	- [ ] 4개 관점이 **모두 동의**하는 구성 요소가 최소 5개 이상
130	- [ ] 그 구성 요소들이 핵심 워크플로우 문제를 **정말 해결**하는가?
131	- [ ] Green Zone 구성 요소들이 "이것들만으로도 작동하는 하네스가 되나?"의 답이 "YES"
132	
133	✅ **위험 가정이 포착되었는가?**
134	- [ ] Top 5 위험 가정이 명시됨
135	- [ ] 각 가정마다 "검증 방법"이 구체적임 (예: "실제 실행 테스트", "Claude Code API 문서 확인")
136	- [ ] 위험 가정이 "워크플로우 전체를 무너뜨릴 수 있는" 수준의 것들임
137	
138	### Phase 3 (수렴) 성공 지표
139	✅ **1차 PRD 초안이 실행 가능한가?**
140	- [ ] Green Zone 구성 요소들의 합계 구현 복잡도가 명시되고 **현실적**인가?
141	- [ ] 각 구성 요소의 우선순위 순서가 명확한가?
142	- [ ] 후순위로 미룬 구성 요소들이 **정말 미룰 수 있는** 것들인가?
143	
144	✅ **모든 팀이 서명할 수 있는가?**

## pandas-ta Overview

Pandas Technical Analysis (Pandas TA) is an easy to use library that leverages the Pandas library with more than 130 Indicators and Utility functions. A popular and comprehensive Technical Analysis Library in Python 3 that leverages numba and numpy for accuracy and performance, and pandas for simplicity and bulk processing. The library contains more than 150 indicators and utilities as well as 60 Candlestick Patterns when TA Lib is installed.

## Key Features

Many commonly used indicators are included, such as: Simple Moving Average (sma) Moving Average Convergence Divergence (macd), Hull Exponential Moving Average (hma), Bollinger Bands (bbands), On-Balance Volume (obv), Aroon & Aroon Oscillator (aroon), Squeeze (squeeze) and many more.

EMA12 and EMA26 can be applied using: df["ema12"] = ta.ema(df["close"], length=12, fillna=df.close) df["ema26"] = ta.ema(df["close"], length=26, fillna=df.close). An Exponential Moving Average (EMA) is similar the Simple Moving Average (SMA) except it's weighted to give more recent data higher importance. When the faster moving average crosses above the slower moving average and visa versa provides trading signals.

## Processing Methods

Pandas TA has three primary "styles" of processing Technical Indicators for your use case and/or requirements. They are: Standard, DataFrame Extension, and the Pandas TA Strategy. Each with increasing levels of abstraction for ease of use.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about using launchd for macOS automatic script scheduling with Python:

## Overview of launchd

launchd is Apple's preferred tool for task automation and management on macOS. As of MacOSX 10.4, cron became deprecated in favor of launchd.

## Key Advantages Over Cron

Both cron and launchd are scheduling services, but launchd is Apple's newer system for macOS that can start jobs based on various triggers – not just time. The biggest advantage of launchd is that it does not assume that your computer is always on (as cron does). Therefore, if your Mac is asleep when a scheduled job was supposed to run, it will automatically run when your Mac is awake.

## Python Script Support

launchd can execute any script that can be run from the terminal. This includes scripts written in Python, Perl, Ruby, and other languages.

## Configuration

Instead of using crontab's text files, launchd jobs (or "agents") are stored in XML files with a .plist extension. Your plist files should go in ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ so that they will be loaded automatically when you log in.

For scheduling timing, you can use StartInterval to start the job every n seconds, or StartCalendarInterval to run the job at a specific time and date.
